clue.text: Get one out of despair, perhaps with a good meal

indicators.note: perhaps hints that the letters of despair can be put in another arrangement once something is taken out

parts.note: one is the Roman numeral I

explanation.surface: Cheering someone up from the depths of gloom by treating them to a fine dinner.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Get one out of' tells you to remove I from DESPAIR, leaving DESPAR, and 'perhaps' rearranges those six letters.
explanation.definitionFit: A spread is a lavish meal laid out on the table, a feast.

clue.text: Filth may do good with this

definitions.text: Filth may do good with this

parts.words: Filth may do good with this
parts.note: Filth is British slang for the police, and a sniffer animal working alongside officers helps them catch criminals

explanation.surface: Dirt can somehow be beneficial when paired with this.
explanation.walkthrough: 'The Filth' is British slang for the police, so the clue is not about dirt at all.
explanation.definitionFit: A trained canine helps officers track suspects and find drugs, doing good work for the force.

clue.text: Unfold next compilation when editor's out

indicators.note: the editor's letters stand out, on the outside, wrapping round the other piece

parts.note: ED is the usual abbreviation for editor

indicators.note: a compilation puts the letters of next together in a new order

explanation.surface: Instructions to open out the next anthology while the editor is away.
explanation.walkthrough: 'compilation' rearranges NEXT into XTEN, and 'when editor's out' puts ED on either side of it.
explanation.definitionFit: To extend something folded is to open it out to full length.

clue.text: It's intrepid to follow Wagner's work with the same

parts.note: Der Ring des Nibelungen, Wagner's opera cycle, is called Der Ring for short
DO is short for ditto, meaning the same again

explanation.surface: Something brave follows on from a Wagner opera, and then repeats itself.
explanation.walkthrough: DO, short for ditto, is a crossword staple for 'the same'.
explanation.definitionFit: Derring-do is bold, daring action, the conduct of an intrepid hero.

clue.text: A sneeze may call for it

definitions.text: A sneeze may call for it

parts.words: A sneeze may call for it
parts.note: a sneeze sends you reaching for a paper handkerchief

explanation.surface: Something needed when someone sneezes.
explanation.definitionFit: A soft paper handkerchief is what someone grabs after a sneeze.

clue.text: Cancer? There's no right to make it a talking point

indicators.note: there's no says a letter is missing from the word that went before

parts.note: the Tropic of Cancer is the line of latitude north of the equator

explanation.surface: A grim diagnosis is something nobody has the right to turn into gossip.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Cancer' suggests illness, but it points to the Tropic of Cancer; 'There's no right' removes R.
explanation.definitionFit: A topic is a subject for discussion, something people talk about.

clue.text: Enlightenment for the masses?

parts.note: read lighten as making less heavy, and masses as bodily bulk: the process of shedding weight

explanation.surface: Spreading education and wisdom to the ordinary people.
explanation.walkthrough: Enlightenment suggests learning, but read it as becoming lighter, and masses as bulky bodies.
explanation.definitionFit: Dieting to lose weight makes a heavy body lighter.

clue.text: Extreme result rarely includes it

indicators.note: includes it says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: An extreme outcome seldom happens.
explanation.definitionFit: Ultra is a prefix and adjective meaning beyond the normal, going to excess.

clue.text: Support best Labour leader or else …

indicators.note: else suggests otherwise, so the letters are made into something different
the leader of a word is its first letter

explanation.surface: A political slogan urging people to back the best Labour leader, or face the consequences.
explanation.walkthrough: BEST, L (first of Labour) and OR are rearranged, signalled by 'else'.
explanation.definitionFit: To bolster is to prop up or reinforce, giving support.

clue.text: Last of 2 finds advantage hard in spring

indicators.note: in places the following pieces within the word for spring

parts.note: to bound is to spring or leap
an asset is something valuable, an advantage
H is the abbreviation for hard, as on pencils

explanation.surface: A clue promising that the end of the second item yields benefit if you try hard in springtime.
explanation.walkthrough: 2-down is POLICE DOG, so 'Last of 2' is the dog part: the definition is a dog.
explanation.definitionFit: A basset hound is a breed of dog, the last word of the answer to 2-down.

clue.text: What's done with tip in order to make it sharp?

indicators.note: putting letters in order means arranging them afresh

explanation.surface: A question about what you do to a pencil tip to make it sharp.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in order' rearranges the letters of DONE and TIP together.
explanation.definitionFit: Something pointed has a sharp tip, coming to a point.

clue.text: Take off 4 and see with logic

parts.note: to deduct is to take off or subtract
IV is four in Roman numerals
Ely is a cathedral city, the seat of a bishop's see

explanation.surface: A maths instruction: subtract four and look, all reasoned out.
explanation.walkthrough: '4' looks like a reference to 4-down but is just IV; a see is a diocese, and Ely is the usual one.
explanation.definitionFit: Deductively means by reasoning from premises to a conclusion, that is logically.

clue.text: Sidekick has pay curtailed — after getting tick fellow has a bit of debt

indicators.note: after getting says the trimmed pay piece follows the tick piece

parts.note: a tick is a moment, a second

indicators.note: curtailed means cut short, losing its last letter

parts.note: income is pay or earnings
a man is a fellow

indicators.note: a bit of takes just the first letter of the next word

explanation.surface: A deputy's wages are cut after buying on credit, and now he owes money.
explanation.walkthrough: 'tick' is not credit but SECOND; 'curtailed' cuts INCOME to INCOM; 'a bit of debt' is D.
explanation.definitionFit: A sidekick is a subordinate partner, the deputy just below the leader.

clue.text: Bear loses head in a whirl

indicators.note: loses head means the first letter is dropped

parts.note: a teddy is a toy bear

explanation.surface: A bear spinning round and losing its head.
explanation.walkthrough: 'loses head' drops the T from TEDDY.
explanation.definitionFit: An eddy is a swirl of water or air, a small whirlpool.

clue.text: Selfish type not go for a hundred? He'd be an oddball

indicators.note: go for a hundred means go replaces the letter for a hundred

parts.note: an eccentric is an oddball, someone unconventional
C is the Roman numeral for a hundred
taken as written

explanation.surface: A self-centred person who did not score a century would be thought odd.
explanation.walkthrough: Put GO in place of one C (a hundred) in ECCENTRIC; without that swap ('not') he would just be an oddball.
explanation.definitionFit: An egocentric is a person absorbed in himself, a selfish type.

clue.text: One might utter rich store of 21s

definitions.text: One might utter rich store of 21s

indicators.note: utter, read as a verb, suggests the letters are spoken out in a fresh order

explanation.surface: A singer could voice a plentiful supply of chants.
explanation.walkthrough: 'utter' rearranges RICH STORE; 21-down is CHANT, so the singer has a store of chants.
explanation.definitionFit: A chorister sings in a church choir, voicing chants.

clue.text: Performance may be extraordinary and shameful

definitions.meaning: a performance of a song or piece is a rendering of it
extraordinary ... is the disgraced practice of secretly moving suspects to be interrogated abroad

explanation.walkthrough: Extraordinary rendition was the secret transfer of terror suspects to other countries for interrogation.
explanation.definitionFit: A rendition is an interpretation or performance of a work.

clue.text: I attempt to include part exchange without change

indicators.note: to include means the first pieces hold the next one inside

parts.note: a try is an attempt
some means a part of something

explanation.surface: Someone tries to get a part-exchange deal on a car without paying any extra.
explanation.walkthrough: 'part exchange' reads as a car trade-in deal, but the phrase splits: 'part' is fodder for the insertion signalled by 'to include', and 'exchange without change' is a mathematician's definition.
explanation.definitionFit: In geometry an isometry is a transformation that keeps all distances the same, a swap of position with no change of shape.

clue.text: Gosh! Big's no way to describe it, though it's important in theory

indicators.note: saying the words are no way to describe it hints they must be put another way, rearranged

parts.note: the letters of Big's taken as written, with its S

explanation.surface: Someone exclaims that calling it big hardly does justice to a theoretically crucial thing.
explanation.walkthrough: GOSH, BIGS and NO are rearranged, signalled by 'way to describe it'.
explanation.definitionFit: The Higgs boson is the particle predicted by physics theory to give others mass.

clue.text: Not in favour of infantile partiality?

indicators.note: partiality is read as part of, so a part of the word is taken

explanation.surface: Questioning whether opposing childish favouritism is the right stance.
explanation.walkthrough: 'partiality' looks like bias, but it signals a part of 'infantile'.
explanation.definitionFit: Anti means against, opposed to something.

clue.text: Element of meal — except one taken with hesitation

parts.note: bar means except, as in all bar one
one is the Roman numeral I
um is a sound of hesitation

explanation.surface: Part of a dinner, apart from one thing eaten while dithering.
explanation.walkthrough: A barium meal is a drink of barium given before an X-ray.
explanation.definitionFit: Barium is a chemical element, swallowed as a 'meal' for X-rays.

clue.text: Lacking transparency, like a so-called public inquiry?

definitions.meaning: not open or forthcoming with information
an official inquiry billed as public may in fact tell the people nothing

explanation.walkthrough: The second part is a wry dig at official inquiries that reveal little.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone uncommunicative keeps things to himself, the opposite of open or transparent.

clue.text: How church worker can offer praise?

parts.note: an ant is the classic worker insect

explanation.surface: Asking how someone who works for a church could give praise.
explanation.walkthrough: 'worker' is the crossword's usual ANT.
explanation.definitionFit: To chant is to sing or intone, as in praising God.

clue.text: Turn over at Waterloo?

definitions.meaning: Waterloo is a London terminus, the far end of the line for trains heading up to the capital

explanation.walkthrough: In Britain trains towards London are 'up' trains, so the London terminus at Waterloo is where the up line ends.
explanation.definitionFit: To upend something is to turn it upside down.

clue.text: One called up for floater in river

indicators.note: in places the floater within the river

parts.note: the Dee is a river in Wales, England and Scotland
a raft is something that floats

explanation.surface: Someone summoned to serve exchanged for a float on the river.
explanation.walkthrough: 'called up' means conscripted to military service.
explanation.definitionFit: A draftee is a person conscripted into the armed forces, called up.

clue.text: Religious doctrine — go to get in it the same

indicators.note: to get in means the next words go inside the attempt

parts.note: a go is a try or attempt
taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: Advice that a religious belief is something to try to understand all the same.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to get in' is the insertion signal; 'the same' just says the doctrine is to be tried regardless, adding no letters.
explanation.definitionFit: The Trinity is the Christian teaching of God as Father, Son and Holy Spirit.

clue.text: Wandered right out — as one might otherwise have done

definitions.text: as one might otherwise have done

indicators.note: out means the letter is taken away

parts.note: strayed means wandered off

explanation.surface: Someone wandered off rightly, when they could have done otherwise.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition plays on the answer: had they not strayed, they would have remained.
explanation.definitionFit: Remaining put is the alternative to wandering off, which is what one might have done instead.

clue.text: Memory with which anyone is inclined to wander

parts.note: ROM is read-only memory in computing
any is short for anyone, as in any will do

explanation.surface: A recollection that makes anyone's mind drift.
explanation.walkthrough: ROM is computer memory; the Romany people were traditionally travellers.
explanation.definitionFit: The Romany are traditionally a travelling, nomadic people, so the word describes a roving life.
